data_diagnostic.reading: The play data contains real manipulation -- 9.8% of action components are at the limit and the state moves substantially -- so the demonstrations are not inert.

decision.cheaper_prior_check: Before or instead of stage 2: re-evaluate the EXISTING checkpoints on goal-distance-matched episodes (the D1-cube ablation). This needs no training, costs well under 0.5 GPU-h, and directly tests whether the zero is caused by goal-distribution shift rather than by the policy class.
decision.do_not_conclude: Do NOT conclude that low-NFE generative modeling fails on compositional manipulation. The evidence supports only that BC without a critic fails on cube-triple at this budget, for every NFE including the non-generative floor.
decision.stage_2_gaussian_diffusion: STILL JUSTIFIED as a falsification check, but now with a second purpose: if Gaussian@100 also scores zero under the same goal shift, the shared cause is the setup rather than the sampler. ~0.4 GPU-h train + ~0.6 eval.
decision.stage_3_shortcut: NOT JUSTIFIED: the NFE axis is flat at zero, so a second low-NFE objective cannot discriminate anything.

evaluation.paired: all arms evaluated on the identical seed set and episode indices
evaluation.success_predicate: official OGBench info['success'] (all three cubes within 0.04 m)

goal_distribution_diagnostic.description: Standardized L2 between the conditioning current state and the conditioning goal, for training-relabeled goals versus the official evaluation task goals.
goal_distribution_diagnostic.reading: Evaluation goals sit at the 88th percentile of the training goal distribution on average, and 17 of 60 exceed the training p95. They are in-support (none exceed the training maximum) but systematically harder than the goals the policy was trained to reach. This is a train/eval goal distribution shift that is NOT controlled in the current protocol, and it is an alternative explanation for zero success that does not implicate the policy class.
goal_distribution_diagnostic.resolution: experiments/pilots/d1_cube_results_v1.json: EASY and HARD subsets both give 0/40 for every arm, and OGBench task 4 -- whose goals are ~40% physically closer than tasks 2/3 -- also yields zero with no distance reduction. Goal difficulty is not the operative cause.

interpretation.closed_loop_failure: With fitting, action saturation, near-misses, and goal difficulty all excluded, the remaining explanation is closed-loop control: the policies emit in-distribution actions but do not compose them into cube movement over a 1000-step episode.
interpretation.consistent_with_literature: Every published cube-triple result uses a critic: FMQ 0.88 with online fine-tuning and NFE 20-32 at test time, MVP with Q-guided generate-and-select, QC Q-learning throughout. Our result is the pure-BC point that was previously unmeasured, and it is near zero.
interpretation.cubes_barely_move: Mean per-cube distance to target goes 0.271 -> 0.266 m at 4 NFE against a 0.04 m success threshold; no cube is ever placed.
interpretation.headline: Under pure behavior cloning at 50k steps, no arm places any cube on cube-triple: 0/60 for BC@1 and for Flow at every NFE tested.
interpretation.nfe_is_not_the_variable: Success is identically 0/60 at 1, 2, 4 and 8 NFE, and identically 0/60 for the non-generative BC floor. The NFE axis is completely flat, so it cannot discriminate anything on this task in this setting. Planner latency scales as expected (2.85 / 5.49 / 10.99 / 20.96 ms), confirming the NFE budget was really spent -- the flatness is not an instrumentation artifact.
interpretation.not_a_fitting_failure: Offline action MAE is 0.116 (BC) and 0.145 (Flow) against an action scale of |mean| 0.297 / std 0.418.
interpretation.not_action_saturation: Action clipping is 2.4-5.4% of steps, far below the 82.9% seen in the earlier puzzle diagnostic.

limitations: one training seed (42); no training-seed uncertainty
50,000 optimizer steps, not a converged budget
60 episodes per arm across three tasks
no critic baseline was run, so BC-vs-critic is inferred from published work rather than measured here
evaluation goals are systematically harder than training goals (88th percentile); this confound is unresolved and weakens any claim that BC per se cannot do the task

offline_diagnostic.description: Normalized action MAE on 256 held-out validation windows, excluding the adapter's zeroed terminal action.
offline_diagnostic.reading: Both models predict actions well below the action scale, so they fit the demonstration distribution. Task failure is therefore not a fitting failure.

statistical_bounds.claimable: 'No arm exceeds ~5% success on cube-triple under this training budget and goal distribution' is supported. 'Behavior cloning cannot solve cube-triple' is NOT supported: it would require multiple training seeds, a converged budget, and control of the goal-distribution shift.
statistical_bounds.method: exact one-sided Clopper-Pearson upper bound for zero successes

per_arm_0_of_60.reading: each arm's true success rate is below ~4.9% at 95% confidence, not provably exactly zero

pooled_0_of_300.reading: pooling all five arms bounds the rate below ~1%, but all arms share ONE training seed, so this is evaluation-episode confidence only and carries no training-seed uncertainty
